content:
While writing the recursion theorem in set theory, I've kept in mind that someone in the future might try to merge recursion in set theory and arithmetic together, due to correspondences in how they're constructed, for example, IsAttempt in set theory corresponds to CSeq in arithmetic. For this reason I'm trying to base my work in SetTheory/Recursion/Blueprint.lean off of work already done in Arithmetic/HFS/PRF.lean.

One difference is that in set theory, Construction.IsAttempt takes an extra argument α compared to Construction.CSeq, because c.IsAttempt v α f also states that domain f equals α. I tried removing length arguments from Recursion.lean instead, but it quickly got difficult. Is it worth changing CSeq to have a length argument in case someone tries to merge it with IsAttempt in the future?

I think it is hard to merge PRF.lean and Recursion.lean, because they are inherently different (specially for complexity/definability). But I wonder why removing length function from Recursion.lean is difficult. Is it due to behaviors of limit ordinals?

I think it is hard to merge PRF.lean and Recursion.lean, because they are inherently different

Okay, thanks! I will worry less about PRF.lean and Recursion.lean growing in different directions.

But I wonder why removing length function from Recursion.lean is difficult. Is it due to behaviors of limit ordinals?

I don't remember limit ordinals specifically being a part of the issue, but instead when I got to ExistsAttempt F α I realized that removing the length argument would make it the predicate ExistsAttempt F, which doesn't give any information about α. I guess I could have replaced its definition with ∃ f : V, IsAttempt F f ∧ domain f = α, but I mist not have thought of that at the time.

I'm also thinking about merging Recursion.lean into Blueprint.lean, which would remove ℒₛₑₜ-function₁ F and instead rely on the formula p.graph, which is related to this part:

(specially for complexity/definability)

C7X said:

I don't remember limit ordinals specifically being a part of the issue, but instead when I got to ExistsAttempt F α I realized that removing the length argument would make it the predicate ExistsAttempt F, which doesn't give any information about α. I guess I could have replaced its definition with ∃ f : V, IsAttempt F f ∧ domain f = α, but I mist not have thought of that at the time.

I think it is better to use ∃ f : V, IsAttempt F f ∧ lh f = α because lh guarantees α is ordinal. Also, this is very similar to PRF.lean.

I did start a branch for (1) removing length arguments and (2) merging Recursion.lean into Blueprint.lean, but I think I'll stop both these efforts for two reasons:

  1. I shouldn't worry about future developers trying to merge PRF.lean and Recursion.lean, since as you had said "I think it is hard to merge PRF.lean and Recursion.lean, because they are inherently different",
  2. ZF.lean has support for using both an ℒₛₑₜ-function₁ F (using repl) and for using a graph sentence (using Blueprint.) I thought it would be a good idea to support both for recursion too.

With this in mind, I have a question about:

I think it is better to use ∃ f : V, IsAttempt F f ∧ lh f = α because lh guarantees α is ordinal. Also, this is very similar to PRF.lean.

Since this advice not applicable if I decided to keep length arguments in IsAttempt, do you mean that I should continue with (1) above?
Yes. Even if we don't merge it, I think that approach would be better because it provides methodological consistency.
